hypothesis: A fresh directional price breakout is more persistent when 7-day realized volatility has risen above and steepened against its 42-day state.
falsifier: Reject the thesis if the baseline lacks cost-resistant edge, fold breadth, or sign specificity, or if removing the volatility-curve transition does not weaken it.
formation_horizon: 56 calendar days, including 7-day and 42-day realized volatility, a 7-day curve lag, a 14-day closing-price channel, and a 7-day event window
rebalance_horizon: Monday 00:00 UTC in every even-numbered ISO week
control_profile: Market-neutral matched long/short selection, fixed 0.15 name weights, at most three names per side, 15% volatility target, drawdown brakes, and 0.20 one-way turnover limit
